summary: On 2 June 2019 a routine maintenance event, a rare misconfiguration and a bug in maintenance automation descheduled network control plane jobs in several locations at once. Network capacity collapsed for hours.

overview.background: Google's network control plane runs as jobs on cluster management instances. Maintenance automation normally deschedules jobs in one location at a time.
systems: Cluster management instances and maintenance automation
Compute Engine, App Engine, Cloud VPN, Cloud Interconnect
Cloud Storage, Spanner, Pub/Sub, BigQuery, G Suite
overview.impact: Compute Engine, App Engine and Cloud VPN were unavailable in us-east4, us-west2, northamerica-northeast1 and southamerica-east1. Cloud Storage error rates reached 96.2 percent in us-west2. Spanner was unavailable in three regions.
overview.severity: Google calls it a major outage in scope and duration. The page lists impact until about 15:40 to 16:10 US/Pacific.
overview.gaps: The page lists the incident end as 15:40 but says full service resumed at 16:10.

diagrams.title: Several control planes descheduled at once
diagrams.caption: Three factors combined: control plane jobs stop during maintenance, their hosts were eligible for a rare maintenance event type, and a bug let the automation deschedule many clusters at once.

timelineNote: Times are as published by the source. Entries without a clock time are given in order only.

timeline.e: A maintenance event starts in one physical location.
Engineers are alerted two minutes after the failure begins.
A status post says Google is investigating a networking issue.
The root cause is identified and the automation software is halted.
A new network configuration begins rolling out.
Full service resumes per the report.

rootCause.trigger: A maintenance event started and the automation descheduled control plane jobs.
rootCause.underlying: Control plane jobs were configured to stop during maintenance, the cluster management instances were eligible for a rare event type, and a bug let the automation deschedule independent clusters in several locations at once.
contributing: A specific software bug in the automation
BGP routes were withdrawn when the control plane stopped
Tools for recovery and communication were also affected

evidence.label: The combination
evidence.body: Two normally-benign misconfigurations, and a specific software bug, combined to initiate the outage

evidence.label: The scale
evidence.body: This was a major outage, both in its scope and duration.

evidence.label: A simulated automation guard
evidence.body:
if len({job.cluster for job in request.jobs}) > 1:
    reject('maintenance may touch one cluster at a time')
evidence.note: A teaching example of the missing rule. Not Google code.

diagnose.step: Find what changed or ran in the first minutes.
Check whether control plane jobs are running in each location.
Look at which regions lost capacity and which kept it.

correct.why: Google did this once it knew the cause.

correct.step: Roll out a new network configuration.
Bring services back region by region.

verify.step: Watch capacity and packet loss in each region.

prevent.step: Reject maintenance requests that affect many clusters.

prevent.why: Routes survive longer outages of the control plane.

fix.safety: Halting maintenance automation globally has its own costs, for example patches are delayed. Plan the restart of automation with safeguards in place.

troubleshoot.scenario: Network capacity is dropping across several regions at once. A maintenance event began in one location a few minutes ago.
clues: Your tools run over the same network
troubleshoot.question: How do you respond?
hints: How do you talk to people if tools are down?
troubleshoot.answer: Halt maintenance automation, restore the control plane, roll out the network configuration, and use an out-of-band channel for communication.

rootcause.q: What combined to cause the outage?
options: Two benign misconfigurations and an automation bug

remediation.answer: Deny maintenance that targets more than one independent cluster or location at a time.
A system keeps using its last known good state when its control plane is unavailable.
Use a status channel that does not use the affected network.

design.prompt: Design maintenance automation that cannot touch several failure domains at once.
design.answer: Enforce one domain at a time, rate limit, require approval for rare event types, and test it with fault injection.

checks.q: What was withdrawn when the control plane stopped?
checks.why: Google says BGP routing was withdrawn.

checks.q: What was Cloud Storage error rate in us-west2?

preventive: Limit automation to one failure domain

verification: Facts were read from Google's incident page on 29 October 2026. The page has a time conflict (15:40 or 16:10), noted. The code is Simulated.
